deep.reconstruction:
Folio 9r has no written derivation. It holds two drawings plus later archival notes: 'Nr. 4851', 'Verschiedene Rechnungen', 'Math. 26' and a foliation number.

(1) LEFT FIGURE (ink, ruled).
- Five outer points form a convex but very irregular pentagon. Approximate image positions are (558,145), (133,278), (27,515), (325,1005) and (636,523).
- All five diagonals are drawn. Their pairwise intersections near the middle give a second, smaller pentagon, with vertices near (268,345), (170,412), (197,517), (455,520) and (475,448).
- The construction is then repeated: the diagonals of the inner pentagon give a third pentagon, and so on. One can see three or four nested generations shrinking into a thin, elongated sliver near (300,440).
- In modern terms this is iteration of the map P -> P' (vertices of P' = intersections of the diagonals of P). This is the 'pentagram map'. For a convex pentagon P', and every later iterate, is projectively equivalent to P, and the iterates collapse to a point.
- The shapes visibly flatten while shrinking. That is consistent with an affinely degenerating but projectively stable shape.
- No numbers or text go with the figure, so whatever Gauss wanted from it (a pure drawing, a test of projective equivalence, or a check of the five-point/pentagon area relation) cannot be read off this page.

(2) RIGHT FIGURE (pencil, much fainter, partly rotated text).
- It is a star of straight lines through roughly a common central region. Some lines run off to long pointer arms with labels.
- The legible labels are sums of pairs drawn from five quantities A,B,C,D,E: A+B, B+C, C+D, D+E, E+A (adjacent pairs) and A+D, B+E, C+A, D+B, E+C (non-adjacent pairs). Together these are all ten 2-element sums of a 5-cycle.
- There are also small annotations that look like differences or expressions such as 'a-b', and possibly numerical values, but they are illegible.

Context:
- The previous page (8v) holds 'Das Pentagon': ten angles A,b,C,d,E,a,B,c,D,e with their log tan, log sin and log cos. They pair up as complements: A+a = b+B = C+c = d+D = E+e = 90°. This is typical of Gauss's Napier-type rules for a pentagram mirificum (self-polar spherical pentagon).
- The next page (9v) computes a pentagon in complex coordinates, with feet of perpendiculars from o and angle computations.
- So the right figure is most plausibly a graphical aid (e.g. a central/gnomonic plot of directions) for the same pentagon problem. The lines would be labeled by the angle sums that occur in the pentagon relations.
- I cannot reconstruct any equation from it with certainty. Anything beyond 'a diagram labeled with the 10 pairwise sums of five quantities' is my interpretation.
errors: No computations on this page to check. The left figure appears accurately ruled: the inner vertices lie on the drawn diagonals as far as resolution allows.
The right-figure labels are too faint for any numerical verification.

results.what: Repeated construction of the pentagon formed by the diagonal intersections of a pentagon (nested pentagons collapsing to a point)
results.modern_name: Pentagram map (iterated diagonal pentagon); projective equivalence of a pentagon and its diagonal pentagon
results.usually_credited_to: R. Schwartz (1992) for the pentagram map as a dynamical system. The projective self-similarity of pentagons is classical; Clebsch and Gauss's pentagramma mirificum are often cited as precursors.

results.what: Diagram labeled with all ten pairwise sums A+B,...,E+C of five pentagon quantities, accompanying the 'Pentagon' angle tables
results.modern_name: Napier-type relations for the pentagramma mirificum (self-polar right-angled spherical pentagon)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (pentagramma mirificum, Nachlass, Werke III/VIII), with Napier's rules as the background

deep.surprise_reason: These are drawings only, without text. Gauss's pentagon work (pentagramma mirificum, the pentagon area formula) is well known. An explicit drawing of the iterated diagonal-pentagon construction is a mildly interesting precursor image of the pentagram map. Nothing here shows he studied its dynamics or invariants.
transcription_corrections: The left figure (not mentioned in the transcription) is a pentagon with its diagonals drawn, iterated: nested diagonal pentagons converge to a thin central sliver.

The right-figure label list should contain exactly the ten pairwise sums of A..E: adjacent A+B, B+C, C+D, D+E, E+A and diagonal A+D, B+E, C+A, D+B, E+C. The extra '[?]' entries (D+B, C+B, E+B, A+C) are probably repeated or misread copies of these.
'Nr. 4851', 'Verschiedene Rechnungen' and 'Math. 26' are archival/later annotations, not Gauss's mathematics. The page also carries a folio number (9) and a library stamp.
